preamble: Loss of glottalization in the glottalized labio-velar approximant [wˀ] (Americanist w̓). It is part of the general loss of glottalized resonants in three neighbouring families of the Northwest Coast. In Makah the Proto-Southern-Wakashan glottalized sonorants merged with the plain ones, with compensatory lengthening of the preceding vowel (Davidson 2002: 76, citing Jacobsen 1968): Nuu-chah-nulth cuw̓it, Makah cu·wit 'silver salmon'. Upriver Halkomelem lost resonant glottalization, usually lengthening the preceding vowel, while Island and Downriver keep it (Compton & Gerdts 2005). In Quileute the Proto-Chimakuan glottalized resonants became plain, sometimes leaving a glottal stop before the resonant (Powell 1974, as summarized on Wikipedia). Chemakum instead hardened *w̓ to (ʔ)kʷ.
